name: tabular_imbalance_resample_bad
title: The same fraud table imputed, power-transformed and ADASYN-oversampled before the split, with the threshold swept against the test labels
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the defective half of the imbalance pair

expected.defect: the mean imputer is fitted on the whole feature matrix eight lines before the split
expected.why: every imputed cell in the training half is filled from a mean the held-out rows helped compute

expected.defect: the Yeo-Johnson transform is fitted on the whole feature matrix before the split
expected.why: the lambda that reshapes every training column was chosen with the held-out rows in it, so the training distribution already knows the test distribution

expected.defect: cross_val_score is handed a bare LogisticRegression over `features`, which prepare() had already imputed, transformed and oversampled outside any fold
expected.why: no fold refits any of the three steps, so the cross-validated average precision is optimistic by the same amount in every fold and the leak is invisible in the fold spread

expected.defect: accuracy_score is handed the probability column from predict_proba(...)[:, 1] instead of a decision
expected.why: a continuous vector is compared to 0/1 labels, so on a 1:400 problem the reported accuracy is meaningless in a way that still looks like a number

expected.defect: roc_auc_score is handed model.predict(...), a hard 0/1 label
expected.why: the ROC curve then has two points and the number is balanced accuracy wearing an AUC label - on an imbalanced problem that is the one place the difference is largest
the split moves every run, and so do the synthetic ADASYN rows that were already in it

expected.defect: nothing seeds random or numpy, the forest carries no random_state and ADASYN draws its neighbours at random
expected.why: two consecutive runs disagree about the threshold as well as about the score

forbidden.why: nothing is fitted on test_x here: the imputer and the transform were both fitted on the whole matrix before the split, which is MLV101's defect, and re-blaming it as MLV102 would be two findings for one root cause
hour_of_day is an integer hour-of-day feature; nothing parses a date, converts one or sorts by one, so there is no temporal signal and MLV106 would be citing evidence that is not there
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no sklearn equivalent
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a scikit-learn program
no device is ever named in this project
nothing is pickled or loaded here

notes: Two planted defects are unsupported, not missed. (1) ADASYN at train.py:48 oversamples before the split, so interpolated copies of training rows land in the test half - that is MLV104, catalogued but not implemented, and it is the single worst defect in this file. (2) tune_threshold_on_test at lines 66-74 sweeps nineteen thresholds against the test labels and keeps the best, which is model selection on the reported set - MLV107, also catalogued but not implemented.
